title: West Virginia Disaster Field Readiness, Forensic Crosswalk & 55-County Regional Kit
subtitle: 2 CFR Part 200 · FEMA PAPPG Category A/B · 33 CFR Parts 203/208 · W. Va. Code § 15-5 · 55-County SEOC Matrix
issuingContext: County Commissions · Emergency Services Directors · Purchasing & Fiscal Clerks · WVEMD Area Liaisons

binderTabs.title: Tab 0: Start Here & Deobligation Traps
binderTabs.summary: Plain-language orientation for County Commissions, Emergency Services Directors, and Fiscal Clerks on the six procurement and monitoring errors that trigger FEMA Public Assistance (PA) deobligations years after floodwaters recede.

tools.title: Top 6 FEMA PA Debris Deobligation Traps (Executive Red-Line Card)
tools.summary: Identifies the six recurring errors in county flood recovery that convert 75%–90% federal cost-share grants into 100% local general-fund clawbacks during OIG post-closeout audits.
tools.trapWarning: Allowing a debris hauler to run past 70 hours on Time-and-Materials (T&M), piggybacking onto another county contract without an assignability clause and cost analysis, or letting haulers write their own load tickets.
steps: Cap emergency Time-and-Materials (T&M) road-clearing ("cut-and-toss") strictly at 70 operating hours with a written Not-To-Exceed (NTE) dollar ceiling.
Never use geographic local-preference scoring on federally reimbursed RFPs (prohibited under 2 CFR § 200.319(c)).
Capture a timestamped SAM.gov active/non-debarred PDF screenshot BEFORE executing any prime or subcontractor award (2 CFR § 180.300).
Separate debris hauling contractors from debris load monitors—a contractor may never verify its own cubic yardage or tonnage.
Obtain prior written FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer (FCO) approval and signed Right-of-Entry (ROE) before entering private property.
Secure written WVDEP environmental closeout clearance on every Temporary Debris Management Site (TDMS) prior to final contractor retainage release.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.318(j) (T&M conditions); 2 CFR § 200.319 (Competition); 2 CFR § 180.300 (Debarment check); 44 CFR § 206.224 (Debris removal); FEMA Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG) v5.0.
copyChecklist: [ ] Written T&M suitability determination & hard NTE dollar cap signed before dispatch
[ ] Hard 70-hour T&M cutover timer set in County EOC Action Tracker
[ ] Timestamped SAM.gov exclusion check saved to grant folder before contract signature
[ ] Independent debris monitor (or county force-account monitor) assigned separately from hauler
[ ] Zero geographic local-preference language in competitive unit-price solicitation
[ ] Private property entry blocked until written FEMA FCO PPDR approval + signed ROE on file

tools.title: Disaster Phase Decision Clock (T-Minus 72h to 3-Year Retention)
tools.summary: Synchronizes County Commission proclamations, WVEMD WebEOC resource requests, USACE levee closures, T&M cutoffs, and FEMA Grants Portal milestones on a single clock.
tools.trapWarning: Starting commercial debris hauling to disposal sites during the Hour 0–70 emergency push before truck tare weights, gate cameras, and unit-price contracts are active.
steps: T-72h to T-0h: Issue Pre-Disaster County Preparedness Log, inspect 33 CFR § 208.10 floodwall closures/culverts, and photograph pre-storm TDMS baseline.
Hour 0 to Hour 70: Issue Local State of Emergency (W. Va. Code § 15-5-6), log WebEOC mission requests to WVEMD, and restrict emergency crews to public ROW life-safety lane pushing.
Day 4 to Day 30: Transition all hauling to competitive unit-price ($/ton or $/CY) contracts with certified scales, truck tare placards, and independent monitors.
Day 31 to Day 180: Reconcile load tickets 1:1 against scale weights before progress payments; remediate TDMS pads and obtain WVDEP sign-off.
Closeout + 3 Years: Preserve complete digital binder for 3 years FROM the date WVEMD submits the final statewide expenditure report to FEMA (not county final payment date).
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: W. Va. Code § 15-5-6 (Emergency proclamations); 44 CFR § 206.36 (Request for federal assistance); 2 CFR § 200.334 (Retention requirements for records—3 years from recipient final financial report).
copyChecklist: [ ] T-48h: Pre-storm geotagged photos of levees, culverts, and candidate TDMS parcels captured
[ ] H+02: County Commission State of Emergency signed & transmitted to WVEMD Watch Center
[ ] H+70: Emergency T&M push closed out; competitive unit-price hauling task order activated
[ ] D+30: Preliminary Damage Assessment (PDA) Category A & B cost packets uploaded
[ ] D+90: HSEEP After-Action Report / Improvement Plan (AAR/IP) filed per EMPG Manual § 12.10
[ ] Closeout: Calendar reminder set for 3 years AFTER WVEMD statewide grant closeout

tools.title: Local Emergency Proclamation & WVEMD Mutual Aid Routing Gate
tools.summary: Establishes clean statutory routing for County Emergency Services Directors activating intrastate county-to-county mutual aid or interstate EMAC teams via the State EOC.
tools.trapWarning: Self-deploying out-of-state resources directly by phone outside WVEMD / EMAC Req-A authorization voids tort immunity, credential reciprocity, and federal reimbursement.
steps: Execute County Commission (or designated President) local emergency proclamation citing W. Va. Code § 15-5-8 and county EOP.
Submit unmet resource needs into WVEMD WebEOC specifying mission capability (not vendor brand name), delivery coordinates, and local staging POC.
For intrastate mutual aid (W. Va. Code § 15-5-11), record sending jurisdiction personnel logs, equipment hours, and daily ICS-214 activity sheets.
For interstate resources, confirm WVEMD EMAC Req-A signature (W. Va. Code § 15-5-22) before mission mobilization.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: W. Va. Code § 15-5-8 (Local organization for emergency services); § 15-5-11 (Mutual aid arrangements); § 15-5-22 (Emergency Management Assistance Compact—EMAC).
copyChecklist: [ ] Local State of Emergency proclamation signed, dated, and filed with County Clerk
[ ] WVEMD Area Liaison notified & WebEOC incident mission tracking number assigned
[ ] Intrastate mutual aid sign-in roster and ICS-214 unit logs issued at County Staging
[ ] Signed EMAC Req-A verified through WVEMD prior to any out-of-state team deployment

tools.title: Force Account Labor, Fringe & Equipment Segregation Ledger
tools.summary: Prevents payroll and county truck disallowances by separating Category A (Debris Removal) from Category B (Emergency Protective Measures) and regular straight-time from overtime.
tools.trapWarning: Under FEMA PA Category A/B permanent-employee rules, regular straight-time salaries of budgeted county road/maintenance staff are generally ineligible—only overtime is reimbursable unless reassigned under specific policy exceptions.
steps: Issue daily disaster timesheets separating Regular Hours vs. Emergency Overtime Hours by exact task and GPS road segment.
Separate Category B life-safety actions (barricades, evacuations, sandbagging, initial lane push) from Category A debris hauling/disposal.
Log county-owned heavy equipment (graders, backhoes, dump trucks) using official FEMA Schedule of Equipment Rates codes with operator name and active operating hours (standby idle time excluded).
Attach pre-disaster county overtime and fringe-benefit personnel policy adopted prior to the incident.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.430 (Compensation—personal services); 44 CFR § 206.228 (Allowable costs—Force Account labor and equipment); FEMA Schedule of Equipment Rates.
copyChecklist: [ ] Pre-existing County Personnel Overtime & Holiday Policy copied into grant binder
[ ] Separate daily timesheets active for Category A (Debris) vs. Category B (Life Safety)
[ ] Equipment logs record active operating hours, VIN/asset ID, FEMA rate code, and operator
[ ] Idle standby hours stripped from equipment reimbursement claim

binderTabs.title: Tab 1: Pre-Storm & Legacy USACE Levee/Floodwall O&M [33 CFR 208]
binderTabs.summary: Protects West Virginia counties operating floodwalls, levees, NRCS watershed channels, and closure structures—including the 112 tracked legacy structures outside the federal levee database—under 33 CFR Parts 203 & 208.

tools.title: Legacy Flood Control Works & Non-NLD Structure Registry
tools.summary: Maps all local levees, WPA concrete floodwalls, NRCS PL-566 watershed dams/channels, and municipal closures across WV (132 tracked statewide structures; 112 outside the USACE National Levee Database).
tools.trapWarning: Discovering during a flood fight that an older municipal floodwall, concrete channel, or coal-valley crib wall is unlisted in the USACE National Levee Database (NLD) and lacks clear local sponsor O&M records.
steps: Verify every floodwall, earthen embankment, concrete channel, and watershed dam in the county against USACE District (Huntington, Pittsburgh, or Baltimore) and WV State Conservation Committee inventories.
Classify each work by federal nexus: USACE Federal/Non-Federal PL 84-99 Active, NRCS PL-566 Watershed Project, or Local/Legacy Municipal Work.
Record exact GPS endpoints, legal local sponsor (County Commission, Municipality, or Conservation District), and easement access deeds.
Establish an annual joint walk-down with the WVEMD Area Liaison and Regional Soil Conservation District.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 33 U.S.C. § 701n (PL 84-99 Flood Control & Coastal Emergencies); 33 CFR Part 203 (Rehabilitation Assistance); 7 CFR Part 624 (NRCS Emergency Watershed Protection).
copyChecklist: [ ] Complete county register of levees, floodwalls, channels, and watershed dams compiled
[ ] NLD-listed vs. Non-NLD legacy status verified with USACE Huntington/Pittsburgh/Baltimore
[ ] Legal Local Sponsor & right-of-way maintenance easements confirmed on file
[ ] High-water river gauge action stages mapped to each structure

tools.title: 33 CFR § 208.10 Levee, Floodwall & Culvert O&M Inspection Log
tools.summary: Operationalizes the mandatory semi-annual and 90-day federal local-sponsor inspection items required to preserve USACE rehabilitation eligibility and prevent catastrophic embankment piping.
tools.trapWarning: Deferred tree growth (>2 inch trunk diameter on embankments), jammed culvert flap gates, or uninspected animal burrows result in "Inactive" PL 84-99 status—leaving the county 100% financially liable for post-flood levee reconstruction.
steps: Inspect earthen embankments semi-annually (and immediately prior to flood season) for sloughing, settlement, seepage boils, woody vegetation, and burrowing rodent tunnels.
Inspect concrete floodwall monolith joints, waterstops, spalling, and toe-drain outfalls every 90 days per 33 CFR § 208.10(b)/(g).
Cycle every interior-drainage sluice gate, flap gate, and trash rack through full open/close travel and clear accumulated woody drift.
Log dated geotagged photos and superintendent sign-offs into the permanent County Flood Works O&M Binder.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 33 CFR § 208.10 (Local flood protection works; maintenance and operation of structures and facilities—requires inspections at least every 90 days and prior to flood season).
copyChecklist: [ ] Embankment crown and slopes mowed; woody brush/trees removed within 15 ft of toe
[ ] Animal burrows excavated, backfilled with compacted impervious soil, and re-seeded
[ ] Concrete floodwall joints, monolith alignment, and foundation drains inspected
[ ] All flap gates, sluice gates, and culvert trash racks cycled and cleared of debris
[ ] Signed 90-day 33 CFR § 208.10 inspection report filed with dated geotagged photos

tools.title: Pump Station Wet-Well, Generator & Street/Rail Closure Drill Card
tools.summary: Ensures storm pump stations and removable aluminum stop-log / miter-gate floodwall closures can be erected under night/rain conditions before river stage reaches sill elevation.
tools.trapWarning: Missing stop-log gaskets, corroded anchor bolts in highway/railroad sill plates, or stale diesel fuel in pump backup generators during a flash-cresting Tug Fork, Ohio, or Kanawha flood.
steps: Inventory numbered aluminum stop-logs, seals, wrenches, timbers, and sandbag stock in each closure storage locker at least annually.
Conduct a physical erection trial of street and railroad closure structures and verify utility/CSX/Norfolk Southern notification numbers.
Run interior storm-drainage pumps under load, test automatic float switches, and verify 72-hour diesel fuel supply + transfer pump readiness.
Post laminated NWS river-gauge trigger elevations inside the County 911 / EOC Dispatch Center.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 33 CFR § 208.10(c) (Closure structures—annual trial erection & numbered storage); 33 CFR § 208.10(e) (Pumping plants—periodic operational load testing).
copyChecklist: [ ] Stop-logs, bolts, gaskets, and lifting tackle inventoried by closure gate number
[ ] Silt and gravel flushed from street/railroad closure sill slots and bolt sockets
[ ] Storm pumps run under load; backup generator fuel tank >= 85% with biocide treatment
[ ] NWS river-gauge stage triggers posted at County EOC & Public Works garage

tools.title: USACE PL 84-99 Rehabilitation Packet & Pre-Storm Photo Baseline
tools.summary: Prepares the 30-day post-flood USACE Rehabilitation Assistance request package and distinguishes USACE PL 84-99 authority from FEMA PA Category D (Water Control Facilities).
tools.trapWarning: FEMA PA strictly denies Category D repair funding for any flood-control work that falls under the specific statutory authority of USACE PL 84-99 or NRCS—even if the county let its USACE eligibility lapse!
steps: Capture annual geotagged baseline photos of levee crests, riprap revetments, pump headers, and channel walls.
Maintain a continuous 3-year log of county O&M expenditures and inspection reports demonstrating active local stewardship.
Within 30 days after floodwaters recede, submit formal written rehabilitation request to the USACE District Flood Control Emergency Manager (Huntington, Pittsburgh, or Baltimore).
Coordinate joint USACE / NRCS / FEMA / WVEMD site inspection so non-USACE drainage structures are cleanly routed to FEMA Category D or NRCS EWP without duplication denials.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 33 CFR § 203.41–203.49 (Rehabilitation of Flood Risk Management Projects); 44 CFR § 206.226(a) (FEMA exclusion where another federal agency holds primary repair authority).
copyChecklist: [ ] Annual geotagged photo baseline stored offline and in county cloud archive
[ ] 3-year O&M work-order & inspection history ready for USACE verification
[ ] USACE District Emergency Operations 24/7 POC card verified (LRH / LRP / NAB)
[ ] 30-day post-flood written PL 84-99 request template pre-addressed for Commission signature

binderTabs.title: Tab 2: First 72 Hours & 70-Hour T&M Ceiling
binderTabs.summary: Governs the highest-risk 72 hours of a disaster: clearing emergency access lanes without violating the FEMA 70-hour Time-and-Materials cap and standing up Day-1 TDMS gate/scale controls before monitors arrive.

tools.title: Emergency Roadway Cut-and-Toss ("Push") vs. Haul-Out Boundary
tools.summary: Draws a hard operational boundary between emergency life-safety lane opening (Category B "cut-and-toss") and collection/hauling to disposal (Category A).
tools.trapWarning: Loading dump trucks and hauling flood debris to landfills under an emergency T&M hourly contract mixes Category B and Category A without load verification—triggering massive FEMA cost disallowances.
steps: Restrict Hour 0–70 emergency crews strictly to cutting downed trees, pushing mudslides/debris off traveled roadway lanes onto public right-of-way (ROW) shoulders, and opening access to hospitals, 911 towers, water plants, and isolated hollows.

Coordinate road clearing with WVDOH County Headquarters (remembering WVDOH maintains county routes in West Virginia, while municipalities/counties cover municipal streets, parks, public buildings, and approved county debris programs).
Require crew foremen to record GPS start/end points, route numbers, and before/after clearing photos on every shift.
Hold ROW debris piles on public shoulders until competitive unit-price hauling and load monitoring activate.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 44 CFR § 206.225 (Emergency protective measures—Category B); 44 CFR § 206.224 (Debris removal—Category A); W. Va. Code § 17-4-1 (WVDOH state/county road jurisdiction).
copyChecklist: [ ] Written crew directive issued: Cut-and-push to ROW shoulder ONLY (no unmonitored haul-out)
[ ] WVDOH County Superintendent deconfliction call completed for state vs. municipal routes
[ ] Priority life-safety corridors (EMS, hospitals, water treatment, shelters) mapped
[ ] Crew shift logs capture route number, GPS coordinates, equipment hours, and cleared photo

tools.title: Hard 70-Hour Time-and-Materials (T&M) Clock & NTE Ceiling Tracker
tools.summary: Tracks every operating hour and dollar billed under emergency T&M contracts and forces mandatory cutover to competitive unit-price contracts at or before Hour 70.
tools.trapWarning: Under 2 CFR § 200.318(j), a Time-and-Materials contract WITHOUT a hard Not-To-Exceed (NTE) ceiling price is flatly illegal under federal grant law—100% of costs can be disallowed.
steps: Sign a brief written determination BEFORE execution stating why scope uncertainty prevents fixed/unit pricing during the initial life-safety window.
Insert an explicit dollar Not-To-Exceed (NTE) cap in the emergency task order that the contractor exceeds wholly at its own risk.
Assign a county employee to verify crew sign-in/sign-out times and active equipment hours daily.
Terminate T&M billing at or before 70 cumulative operating hours and switch to pre-positioned or emergency-solicited unit-price ($/ton or $/CY) rates.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.318(j)(1)–(2) (Time-and-materials contracts allowed only after determination no other contract is suitable AND if contract includes a ceiling price contractor exceeds at own risk); FEMA PAPPG 70-hour emergency debris benchmark.
copyChecklist: [ ] Written "No Other Contract Suitable" determination signed by County Purchasing Officer
[ ] Explicit dollar Not-To-Exceed (NTE) ceiling written on face of Task Order
[ ] Daily county supervisor verification signature on T&M equipment & labor logs
[ ] Written Stop-Work / Transition Notice issued prior to Hour 70 cumulative mark

tools.title: Day-1 Emergency Gate Camera, Tare Placard & Scale Ticket Standup
tools.summary: Establishes tamper-evident corroborating evidence from Day 1 so if contracted debris monitors take days to mobilize in mountain terrain, early hauling loads remain forensically provable.
tools.trapWarning: Relying solely on contractor-written paper tickets while waiting for a monitoring firm to mobilize creates an "Unmonitored Record Gap" that auditors routinely flag as unsupported.
steps: Mount a fixed, NTP-time-synced digital trail/gate camera at every TDMS exit capturing truck side-placard ID, cab, and open bed load profile on departure.
Weigh every hauling truck empty at a WV Division of Labor certified scale before its first load, photograph VIN + plate + side Truck ID, and record Registered Empty Tare (tons).
Direct all disposal loads exclusively to certified commercial landfills issuing machine-printed gross/tare/net weight tickets with arrival/exit timestamps.
Archive raw gate camera SD/NVR files nightly with SHA-256 checksums so zero frames are overwritten.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.303 (Internal controls—reasonable assurance of compliance and reliable reporting); 2 CFR § 200.403 (Factors affecting allowability of costs—be adequately documented).
copyChecklist: [ ] Fixed NTP-synced camera mounted at TDMS exit gate showing Truck ID + loaded bed
[ ] Every truck weighed empty on certified scale; VIN, plate & tare placard photographed
[ ] Landfill scale house instructed to record Truck ID and machine-printed Gross/Tare/Net tons
[ ] Nightly copy of gate camera photos hashed (SHA-256) and backed up to County Clerk storage

binderTabs.title: Tab 3: 2 CFR Part 200 Contracting, RFPs & Load Monitoring
binderTabs.summary: Ensures county standby and emergency debris procurements pass FEMA Procurement Disaster Assistance Team (PDAT) review and establishes independent load/forensic reconciliation.

tools.title: 2 CFR §§ 200.318–200.327 Competitive RFP & Piggyback Trap Audit
tools.summary: Walks County Purchasing Clerks through competitive solicitation rules, mandatory Independent Cost Estimates (ICE), socioeconomic outreach, and the strict ban on improper piggybacking.
tools.trapWarning: "Piggybacking" onto a neighboring county or out-of-state cooperative contract that lacked an explicit assignability cap, county scope match, or independent cost analysis is the #1 cause of 100% FEMA procurement disallowances.
steps: Prepare a written Independent Cost Estimate (ICE) using historical WVEMD/USACE regional ton/CY rates BEFORE opening bids or proposals (2 CFR § 200.324).
Solicit full and open competition with zero local/in-state geographic preference points (2 CFR § 200.319).
Document all six affirmative socioeconomic outreach steps (sending RFP notice to WV Small, Minority, and Women-owned business directories per 2 CFR § 200.321).
Prohibit cost-plus-a-percentage-of-cost (CPPC) pricing structures under all circumstances (2 CFR § 200.324(d)).
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.319 (Competition); § 200.320 (Methods of procurement); § 200.321 (Contracting with small/minority/women businesses); § 200.324 (Contract cost and price—ICE & CPPC ban).
copyChecklist: [ ] Written Independent Cost Estimate (ICE) signed and dated BEFORE bid opening
[ ] Solicitation scrubbed of all local/county/state geographic preference preferences
[ ] Affirmative outreach emails/notices sent to M/WBE & SBA directories saved to file
[ ] Pricing table uses unit-price ($/ton or $/CY)—zero cost-plus-percentage-of-cost items
[ ] Any cooperative/statewide contract verified for assignability clause + scope/ceiling match

tools.title: SAM.gov Debarment Screen & Appendix II Mandatory Clauses Packet
tools.summary: Verifies contractor eligibility on SAM.gov prior to award and attaches the required federal contract rider to every county purchase order and emergency contract.
tools.trapWarning: Awarding a disaster contract to a suspended/debarred contractor—or omitting SAM.gov proof taken BEFORE contract execution—triggers mandatory non-reimbursement.
steps: Search the exact legal entity name and UEI of the prime contractor and known Tier-1 subcontractors on SAM.gov and print/save the dated PDF result BEFORE signing.

Attach the Federal Appendix II Rider covering Termination for Cause/Convenience (> $10k), Equal Employment Opportunity, Contract Work Hours & Safety Standards (> $100k + mechanics/laborers), Clean Air & Water (> $150k), and Byrd Anti-Lobbying (> $100k).
Include explicit FEMA, DHS OIG, Comptroller General, and WVEMD access-to-records and 3-year record retention clauses.
Include DHS Seal/Logo prohibition and No-Federal-Government-Obligation disclaimers.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 180.300 (Nonprocurement debarment verification); 2 CFR § 200.327 & Part 200 Appendix II (Contract provisions for non-Federal entity contracts under Federal awards).
copyChecklist: [ ] Dated SAM.gov active/zero-exclusion PDF saved BEFORE contract execution timestamp
[ ] Appendix II Federal Contract Rider attached and initialed by vendor
[ ] Contract Work Hours / Overtime safety clause included (for contracts > $100,000)
[ ] Clean Air / Federal Water Pollution Control & Byrd Anti-Lobbying certification signed
[ ] Explicit access-to-records clause for County, WVEMD, FEMA, and DHS OIG included

tools.title: Independent Debris Monitor Separation & Certified Truck Registry
tools.cite: FEMA PAPPG Ch. 7; Debris Monitoring Guide
tools.summary: Establishes conflict-free load verification at pickup, TDMS tower, and final landfill scale—preferring net-tonnage certified scale billing over subjective cubic-yard estimates.
tools.trapWarning: Paying per cubic yard (CY) without physical truck-bed measurement deductions (doghouses, sloped tailgates, sideboards) or hand-loading "air-gap" call-downs routinely inflates claims by 25%–40%.
steps: Staff collection and tower monitoring with either trained county force-account employees or a competitively procured monitoring firm wholly independent of the hauling contractor.
Where certified landfill scales exist within haul range, contract on Net Weight ($/ton) rather than volume ($/CY) to eliminate subjective percent-full disputes.
Maintain a master Truck Certification Ledger: Truck ID, VIN, Plate, Registered Empty Tare (tons), measured bed CY, and 4-side photos.
Require re-certification immediately if sideboards, tailgates, or truck cabs are altered.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.318(b) (Contractor oversight—non-Federal entities must maintain oversight to ensure contractors perform in accordance with terms, conditions, and specifications); FEMA Debris Monitoring Guide.
copyChecklist: [ ] Written conflict-of-interest attestation signed by debris monitoring personnel
[ ] Master Truck Certification Ledger completed before any truck enters haul rotation
[ ] Net-tonnage ($/ton) certified scale billing enforced for C&D and mixed flood debris
[ ] Daily spot-check of empty tare weights against Registered Tare (+/- 0.35 ton tolerance)

tools.title: 6-Check Forensic Record-Gap Reconciliation Protocol
tools.summary: Applies six deterministic physics and identity audits across TDMS gate camera logs, certified landfill scale tickets, and Week 4 monitored benchmarks to separate valid loads from anomalies.
tools.trapWarning: Submitting unvetted contractor invoices from an unmonitored gap period invites DHS OIG statistical extrapolation—where 3 bad tickets can taint an entire multi-week invoice.
steps: Check 1 — Loaded-Trip Time Window: Confirm (Scale Arrival - TDMS Gate Exit) falls within physical minimum (e.g., 32 min) and empirical P95 maximum (e.g., 55 min from Week 4 monitored baseline).
Check 2 — Round-Trip Turnaround: Verify consecutive scale cycles exceed minimum loaded haul + dump + empty return + reload duration (>= 72 min).
Check 3 — Tare Weight Identity Consistency: Flag any scale empty tare deviating > 0.35 tons from the truck's certified registered tare (catches chassis swaps).
Check 4 — Active Fleet Count: Confirm concurrent active trucks per shift never exceed the certified registry count.
Check 5 — Billed vs. Scale Tonnage Match: Reject duplicate scale ticket numbers and any invoice tonnage exceeding certified net scale weight.
Check 6 — Photo Timestamp Continuity: Require an unbroken SHA-256 gate camera exit frame matching every claimed haul load.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.403(a) & (g) (Costs must be necessary, reasonable, and adequately documented); 2 CFR § 200.404 (Reasonable costs—prudent person standard).
copyChecklist: [ ] TDMS gate exit timestamps aligned to NTP clock & matched against landfill scale arrivals
[ ] Week 4 (or monitored window) empirical transit min/max distribution calculated
[ ] All 6 Forensic Checks executed (Transit, Turnaround, Tare, Fleet Count, Scale Match, Photo Hash)
[ ] Anomalous/duplicate loads formally placed on Hold & deducted prior to FEMA reimbursement claim

binderTabs.title: Tab 4: Hazmat, Waterway & Private-Property ROE Debris
binderTabs.summary: Handles high-consequence Appalachian flood debris hazards: displaced propane/chlorine/ammonia cylinders in river valleys (ERG 2024), stream/bridge debris routing, and Private Property Debris Removal (PPDR).

tools.title: Orphan Cylinders, Industrial Tanks & ERG 2024 Valley Isolation Card
tools.summary: Provides verified 2024 Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) isolation zones for flood-displaced cylinders/tanks in narrow WV valleys and EPA refrigerant/HHW segregation rules.
tools.trapWarning: Crushing displaced propane tanks, water-treatment chlorine cylinders, agricultural ammonia tanks, or refrigerator compressors in a C&D grapple causes BLEVE/toxic plume incidents and Clean Air Act violations.
steps: UN1075 Propane / LPG (Guide 115): Small spill isolate 330 ft; large spill isolate 2,640 ft (0.5 mi) & 0.5 mi downwind; tank involved in fire -> isolate 1 mile (1,600 m) all directions (BLEVE risk).

UN1017 Chlorine (Guide 124): Heavy TIH gas that pools in river valleys—small spill isolate 200 ft (0.3 mi day / 1.1 mi night downwind); large spill isolate 1,000 ft (1.9 mi day / 4.9 mi night downwind); shelter-in-place with HVAC off if evacuation crosses plume.

UN1005 Anhydrous Ammonia (Guide 125): Small spill isolate 100 ft (0.1 mi day / 0.2 mi night); large spill isolate 500 ft (0.5 mi day / 1.3 mi night); apply water fog to vapor cloud ONLY—never apply water directly into liquid spill.
UN1170 Ethanol Solutions (Guide 127): Polar solvent requiring Alcohol-Resistant Foam (AR-AFFF); small spill 150 ft; large spill 1,000 ft & 0.5 mi downwind; tank car in fire isolate 0.5 mi.
Segregate Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) on lined/bermed TDMS pads and log certified technician recovery of CFC/HCFC refrigerants from appliances per 40 CFR Part 82.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: U.S. DOT PHMSA 2024 Emergency Response Guidebook (Guides 115, 124, 125, 127); 40 CFR Part 82 Subpart F (EPA Refrigerant Recycling/Recovery); WVDEP Emergency Spill Notification (1-800-642-3074).
copyChecklist: [ ] Spotters briefed on ERG 2024 Guide 115 (Propane), 124 (Chlorine), 125 (Ammonia), 127 (Ethanol)
[ ] Orphan propane/chemical cylinders staged upright in segregated,flagged Hazmat corral
[ ] White goods staged separately; EPA-certified technician CFC/freon extraction log maintained
[ ] WVDEP Spill Line (1-800-642-3074) & Regional Hazmat Team notified of leaking/unmarked drums

tools.title: Waterway, Bridge-Pier Drift & NRCS EWP vs. FEMA PA Routing Matrix
tools.summary: Prevents federal agency turf denials when clearing logjams, gravel bars, and flood-deposited debris from West Virginia creeks, bridge piers, and navigable rivers.
tools.trapWarning: Dredging gravel bars or excavating stream channels with county excavators without WVDEP stream-activity coordination and NRCS vs. FEMA PA eligibility verification risks Clean Water Act § 404 violations and FEMA denial.
steps: Immediate Bridge/Culvert Threat: Debris piled directly against public bridge piers or culvert inlets threatening structural failure qualifies under FEMA PA Category A—photograph exact blockage footprint before removal.

Upland Stream Blockages Threatening Life/Property: Route channel logjams and bank stabilization outside public ROW first to USDA-NRCS Emergency Watershed Protection (EWP) through the Conservation District (7 CFR Part 624).
Navigable Waterways (Ohio, Kanawha, Monongahela, Big Sandy): Coordinate submerged navigation hazards with USACE District and U.S. Coast Guard.
Submit WVDEP / USACE Nationwide Permit #3 / Emergency Stream Activity notice prior to placing tracked machinery below ordinary high-water mark.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 44 CFR § 206.224(a) (Immediate threat to life, public health, or improved property); 7 CFR Part 624 (NRCS EWP—primary federal authority for watershed channel debris); 33 U.S.C. § 1344 (Clean Water Act § 404).
copyChecklist: [ ] Pre-work geotagged photos showing debris directly impinging public bridge pier or culvert
[ ] NRCS State/District Conservationist consulted for EWP channel logjam eligibility
[ ] WVDEP Emergency Stream Activity / USACE NationWide Permit notification logged
[ ] Zero unauthorized streambed gravel mining—removal restricted strictly to flood-deposited drift

tools.title: Private Property Debris Removal (PPDR) & Right-of-Entry (ROE) Gate
tools.summary: Enforces the strict four-step legal gate required BEFORE county contractors set foot on private residential or commercial parcels to remove flood debris or demolish unsafe structures.
tools.trapWarning: Entering private property to haul flood debris WITHOUT advance written approval from the FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer (FCO) results in 100% denial of every load pulled from private land.
steps: Step 1 — Public Health & Legal Authority: Obtain County Health Officer written determination that widespread private debris poses an immediate public health/safety threat, plus County Prosecutor confirmation of local nuisance abatement authority.
Step 2 — Prior Written FEMA FCO Approval: Submit formal PPDR request through WVEMD to FEMA and WAIT for signed FCO authorization specifying approved parcels/zones.
Step 3 — Landowner ROE + Insurance Assignment: Collect signed Right-of-Entry, Hold Harmless, and Homeowner Insurance Duplication-of-Benefits disclosure for each parcel.
Step 4 — Pre-Entry & Post-Clearing Verification: Conduct asbestos/hazmat + historic preservation (SHPO) screening on demolitions and photograph parcel before and after clearing.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 44 CFR § 206.224(b) (Public interest determination for private property debris removal); 44 CFR § 206.250 (Insurance & duplication of benefits under Stafford Act § 312).
copyChecklist: [ ] County Health Officer public-health threat declaration signed
[ ] County Legal Counsel written opinion confirming legal authority to enter/abate nuisance
[ ] Written FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer (FCO) PPDR approval letter received BEFORE work
[ ] Signed Landowner ROE, Hold Harmless, and Insurance Debris Coverage disclosure on file per APN
[ ] SHPO historic check & WVDEP asbestos NESHAP notice completed prior to any structure demolition

binderTabs.title: Tab 5: FEMA PA Reimbursement & Closeout Defense
binderTabs.summary: Locks down final environmental site clearance, Grants Portal 1:1 financial reconciliation, and questioned-cost carve-out defenses so disaster funds stay in the county treasury.

tools.title: TDMS Environmental Baseline, Reduction Logs & WVDEP Final Sign-Off
tools.cite: W. Va. Code § 22-15; FEMA PAPPG Ch. 7
tools.summary: Tracks Temporary Debris Management Site (TDMS) lifecycle from pre-activation soil/water baseline through mulching/incineration reduction to final WVDEP restoration sign-off.
tools.trapWarning: Releasing final contractor retainage before WVDEP issues written TDMS closeout approval leaves the county stuck paying non-reimbursable soil remediation or orphan wood-chip disposal costs.
steps: Document pre-activation TDMS parcel condition with aerial/ground photos and baseline soil/groundwater samples (confirming outside 100-yr floodplain and wetlands).
Track incoming vs. outgoing tonnage/volume at TDMS (verifying realistic ~4:1 vegetative grinding or ~95% air-curtain incineration reduction ratios).
Remove 100% of ash, wood mulch, C&D residue, and HHW containment liners to permitted final disposal facilities within WVDEP emergency authorization deadlines.
Hold minimum 10% contractor retainage until post-use soil testing passes and written WVDEP site closure letter is placed in the FEMA Grants Portal folder.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: W. Va. Code § 22-15 (Solid Waste Management Act); W. Va. Code § 22-5 (Air Pollution Control—Air Curtain Incinerator permits); FEMA PAPPG TDMS Environmental & Historic Preservation (EHP) requirements.
copyChecklist: [ ] Pre-activation TDMS baseline photos, SHPO/floodplain check, and soil baseline logged
[ ] Daily TDMS inbound vs. outbound haul-out ledger balanced (zero orphan mulch piles)
[ ] Post-remediation soil/site inspection completed with WVDEP Environmental Inspector
[ ] Written WVDEP TDMS Final Closure Letter archived BEFORE releasing final 10% retainage

tools.title: Grants Portal Category A Workbook & 1:1 Invoice-to-Scale Reconciliation
tools.summary: Structures the county's FEMA Grants Portal Category A submission so every single dollar claimed traces cleanly from check/ACH cleared date back to scale ticket and GPS pickup sector.
tools.trapWarning: Summary lump-sum contractor invoices ("Debris Removal Week 2 — $145,000") without line-by-line load ticket and scale ticket schedules fail WVEMD Closeout and DHS OIG single-audit testing.
steps: Compile the FEMA Load Ticket Summary Spreadsheet matching 1:1: Invoice #, Line #, Load ID, Date, Truck ID, Registered Tare, Gate Exit Time, Scale Ticket #, Scale Arrival Time, Net Tons, Unit Rate, and Extended Dollar Amount.
Attach bank-cleared check images or ACH remittance proofs showing actual county disbursement prior to final reimbursement closeout (2 CFR § 200.302).
Cross-check insurance proceeds, scrap-metal recycling revenues, and NRCS/USACE work to deduct any credits or Duplication of Benefits (2 CFR § 200.406).
Lock immutable PDF + CSV closeout archive with County Clerk & Emergency Services for >= 3 years post-WVEMD statewide closeout.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.302 (Financial management—accurate, current, and complete disclosure); 2 CFR § 200.334 (3-year record retention from recipient final expenditure report); 2 CFR § 200.406 (Applicable credits).
copyChecklist: [ ] Every contractor invoice line mapped 1:1 to unique Load ID + Certified Scale Ticket #
[ ] Scrap-metal recycling credits & insurance proceeds netted out per 2 CFR § 200.406
[ ] Cleared County Commission warrants / ACH proof of payment attached to each voucher
[ ] Read-only closeout archive indexed and locked for 3+ years post-statewide closeout

tools.title: OIG Audit & Questioned-Cost Carve-Out Defense Strategy
tools.summary: Demonstrates affirmative county internal controls by proactively segregating and withholding payment on anomalous haul tickets while defending verified loads with multi-source corroboration.
tools.trapWarning: When a county submits 100% of an unmonitored invoice including obvious anomalies (19-minute transit times or duplicate scale tickets), reviewers lose trust in the entire dataset and question the whole period.
steps: Run the 6-Check Forensic Crosswalk on any period where tower or roving monitoring had operational gaps.

Issue a formal Contractor Credit Memo / Short-Pay Hold Notice carving out every flagged load (impossible transit, tare swap, duplicate scale ticket, missing gate frame) BEFORE claiming federal reimbursement.

Attach the empirical Monitored Baseline comparison (showing identical truck fleet, route transit median, and net ton distribution) to substantiate the verified loads under 2 CFR § 200.404 Reasonable Cost standards.
Preserve appeal rights under 44 CFR § 206.206 (strict 60-day applicant appeal window via WVEMD from receipt of FEMA determination).
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.404 (Reasonable costs); 2 CFR § 200.405 (Allocable costs); 44 CFR § 206.206 (FEMA PA Appeals—60-day statutory filing deadline).
copyChecklist: [ ] Questioned loads placed on formal Accounting Hold & excluded from FEMA PA claim
[ ] Federal Reviewer Justification Memo generated comparing Gap vs. Monitored Baseline
[ ] Gate camera SHA-256 photo manifest + certified scale house affidavit attached
[ ] 60-day 44 CFR § 206.206 appeal deadline tracked immediately upon any FEMA RFI/DM

binderTabs.title: Tab 6: Plain-Language County Templates & Checklists
binderTabs.summary: Copy-and-print plain-language county operational forms built for courthouse clerks, road supervisors, and volunteer EOC teams operating without internet connectivity.

tools.title: Template A — 70-Hour Emergency Road-Clearance Task Order & NTE Clause
tools.summary: Drop-in county task order language establishing the mandatory T&M suitability finding, hard 70-hour emergency cutoff, and strict dollar Not-To-Exceed ceiling.
tools.trapWarning: Never issue a verbal "clear the roads and send us the bill" instruction—use this 1-page written Task Order even at 2:00 AM during a flash flood.
steps: Fill in County Name, Disaster Proclamation Date, Contractor Legal Name, UEI, and Verified SAM.gov Check Timestamp.
Set a hard Dollar Not-To-Exceed (NTE) Ceiling (e.g., $75,000) and explicit 70-Operating-Hour automatic expiration.
Restrict scope strictly to emergency life-safety roadway push to public ROW—zero haul-away disposal without separate unit-price authorization.
Have both County Commission Representative and Contractor Superintendent sign prior to equipment roll.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.318(j) (Mandatory written suitability determination and ceiling price for Time-and-Materials contracts); W. Va. Code § 15-5-8.
copyChecklist: EMERGENCY 70-HOUR ROADWAY CLEARANCE TASK ORDER (2 CFR § 200.318(j))
SAM.gov Active / Zero-Exclusion PDF Saved At (Date/Time): __________________

1. SUITABILITY FINDING: Due to active flood emergency conditions, exact debris scope cannot yet be estimated accurately; no contract type other than short-term Time-and-Materials is suitable for immediate life-safety roadway opening.
2. SCOPE LIMITATION: Cut-and-push emergency debris off traveled public lanes onto public ROW shoulders ONLY. Zero hauling to disposal under this Task Order.

3. HARD CEILING & 70-HOUR CAP: Total billing shall NOT EXCEED $____________ (NTE Ceiling) and expires automatically at 70 cumulative operating hours. Contractor exceeds this ceiling wholly at its own risk.
4. FEDERAL CLAUSES: Subject to 2 CFR Part 200 Appendix II Rider and County/WVEMD/FEMA/OIG audit access.

tools.title: Template B — County Truck Certification & Empty Tare Placard Log
tools.cite: FEMA PAPPG Debris Monitoring Guide; 2 CFR § 200.303
tools.summary: Standardizes county truck intake at staging so every dump truck, knuckleboom trailer, and roll-off carries a verified empty tare weight and tamper-evident placard.
tools.trapWarning: Allowing magnetic placards to move between trucks or failing to re-weigh after sideboard/tailgate changes breaks Check 3 (Tare Weight Identity Consistency).
steps: Assign sequential adhesive County Placard IDs (e.g., TRK-201+) affixed to both cab doors—prohibit removable magnetic signs.
Record empty weight on a WV Division of Labor certified scale with full fuel tank and driver out/in per standard landfill protocol.
Measure interior bed Length x Width x Height (inches) and subtract doghouse, sloped front, or missing tailgate deductions.
Capture 4 geotagged photos: Front Plate + Cab, Left Placard + Bed, Rear Tailgate + Plate, and Certified Empty Scale Ticket.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 2 CFR § 200.303 (Internal controls); FEMA Public Assistance Debris Monitoring Guide (Truck Certification Standards).

Assigned Adhesive Placard ID: TRK-_______   Date/Time: _____________________
Prime Contractor: _______________________   Subcontractor: _________________
Driver Name: ____________________________   License Plate / State: _________
Certified Scale Empty Tare Weight: _________ Tons  (Scale Ticket #: ________)
Measured Bed (L x W x H in.): _____ x _____ x _____  Net Certified CY: _____
Tailgate Type: [ ] Standard Solid  [ ] Barn Door  [ ] Modified / Deducted
4-Photo Set Saved: [ ] Front  [ ] Left Placard  [ ] Rear Plate  [ ] Tare Ticket
County Certifying Inspector Signature: _____________________________________

tools.title: Template C — Private Property ROE, Hold Harmless & Insurance Disclosure
tools.summary: Plain-language landowner authorization and insurance subrogation form for approved Private Property Debris Removal (PPDR) operations.
tools.trapWarning: Collecting a 1-sentence homeowner signature that omits insurance debris-coverage disclosure exposes the county to Stafford Act § 312 Duplication of Benefits clawbacks.
steps: Confirm FEMA FCO written PPDR approval covers the parcel's street/tax map before distributing ROE forms.
Verify property ownership against County Assessor tax parcel records.
Record homeowner/flood insurance carrier, policy number, and any specific debris-removal rider coverage.
Attach pre-entry parcel photo showing flood debris threat and file signed ROE by Tax Map / Parcel ID.
tools.endnote: Statutory Authority: 44 CFR § 206.224(b) (Private property debris removal); 44 CFR § 206.250 & 42 U.S.C. § 5155 (Stafford Act § 312 Duplication of Benefits prohibition).
copyChecklist: RIGHT-OF-ENTRY (ROE), HOLD HARMLESS & INSURANCE DISCLOSURE FORM

1. RIGHT OF ENTRY: Owner voluntarily authorizes County, WVEMD, FEMA, USACE, and authorized contractors to enter the property solely to remove eligible disaster-generated debris posing a public health/safety hazard.
2. HOLD HARMLESS: Owner releases and holds harmless County, State of West Virginia, and United States Government from incidental damage necessary to accomplish debris removal.

3. NO DUPLICATION OF BENEFITS (42 U.S.C. § 5155): Insurance Carrier: ___________________ Policy #: _______________ Does policy cover debris removal? [ ] Yes [ ] No. Owner assigns any specific debris-removal insurance proceeds to County to prevent federal duplication of benefits.

questions.text: County maintains competitively solicited, pre-positioned standby debris hauling ($/ton and $/CY) contracts ready for task-order activation.
questions.actionItem: Issue a competitive 3-year zero-dollar standby Debris Hauling RFP with unit-price schedules ($/ton & $/CY) so emergency work never drags past 70 hours on T&M.

questions.text: Solicitation file contains a written Independent Cost Estimate (ICE) signed and dated BEFORE bid/proposal opening.
questions.actionItem: Compile a pre-bid Independent Cost Estimate (ICE) benchmarked against historical WVEMD and USACE Huntington/Pittsburgh/Baltimore regional debris unit rates.

questions.text: All six affirmative socioeconomic outreach steps (Small, Minority, and Women-owned business solicitations) are documented in the procurement file.
questions.actionItem: Add mandatory M/WBE & SBA dynamic small-business solicitation emails and split-package evaluation records to the standby procurement packet per 2 CFR § 200.321.

questions.text: Standby and emergency RFP templates contain ZERO local/county/in-state geographic preference scoring or cost-plus-percentage-of-cost pricing.
questions.actionItem: Scrub county purchasing ordinances and disaster RFP templates to strip any local vendor preference points when federal disaster reimbursement may apply.

questions.text: County prohibits informal "piggybacking" onto neighboring county contracts unless explicit assignability, ceiling caps, and independent price analysis exist.
questions.actionItem: Adopt a County Purchasing Red-Line Rule prohibiting piggyback disaster contract awards without prior legal review against FEMA PDAT assignability criteria.

selfCheckPillars.title: 2. Temporary Debris Management Sites & WVDEP Permits
selfCheckPillars.subtitle: W. Va. Code § 22-15 & Environmental Clearance

questions.text: At least two pre-screened county Temporary Debris Management Site (TDMS) parcels are mapped outside the 100-year floodplain and wetlands.
questions.actionItem: Pre-designate primary and backup county-owned or MOU-secured upland TDMS parcels outside FEMA Special Flood Hazard Areas (Zone AE/A).

questions.text: Pre-activation baseline environmental photos and SHPO/endangered-species desktop clearances are stored for each candidate TDMS parcel.
questions.actionItem: Capture annual baseline photos and pre-screen candidate TDMS parcels with WV State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO) and WVDEP Solid Waste Management.

questions.text: WVDEP emergency solid waste staging & Air Curtain Incinerator notification contacts and setback maps (>= 1,000 ft from dwellings/schools) are on file.
questions.actionItem: Pre-file candidate TDMS GPS polygons and vegetative reduction buffer maps with the WVDEP Regional Environmental Enforcement Office.

questions.text: TDMS layout plan enforces physical segregation and lined containment berms for Household Hazardous Waste (HHW), white goods/freon, electronics, and C&D.
questions.actionItem: Stage heavy 6-mil/30-mil poly liners, spill kits, and signage for segregated HHW, orphan propane/chlorine cylinders, and white-goods refrigerant recovery.

questions.text: Hauling contract withholds >= 10% final retainage until written WVDEP TDMS remediation & environmental closure clearance is issued.
questions.actionItem: Add a mandatory 10% closeout retainage hold tied to written WVDEP TDMS site restoration sign-off before final contractor invoice release.

questions.text: Independent debris monitoring contract (or trained county force-account monitor roster) is pre-positioned completely separate from hauling vendors.
questions.actionItem: Pre-qualify an independent debris monitoring vendor OR train 6+ county staff (Assessor/Parks/Code) on FEMA truck certification and tower monitoring.

questions.text: County Truck Certification protocol captures VIN, license plate, adhesive placard ID, 4-angle photos, and certified empty scale tare weight before Haul #1.
questions.actionItem: Stock sequential tamper-evident adhesive truck placards and printed Template B Truck Certification Logs in the County EOC Go-Kit.

questions.text: NTP-time-synchronized TDMS exit gate camera kit is staged to record departing Truck IDs, open bed loads, and SHA-256 photo hashes from Day 1.
questions.actionItem: Stage two rugged solar/battery trail/IP gate cameras in the EOC cache with nightly SHA-256 hash backup script to prevent Day 1–14 unmonitored record gaps.

questions.text: Regional Subtitle D landfills and WV Division of Labor certified truck scales are pre-mapped with haul distance and empirical loaded transit-time bounds.
questions.actionItem: Map exact highway mileage and min/max loaded tri-axle transit minutes from each candidate TDMS to permitted regional Subtitle D landfills.

questions.text: Fiscal office runs automated 6-check forensic reconciliation (transit window, turnaround, tare match, fleet cap, scale match, photo continuity) prior to payment.
questions.actionItem: Require 6-Check Forensic Crosswalk clearance before placing any debris hauling progress invoice on the County Commission payment docket.

selfCheckPillars.title: 4. Legacy Flood Control / USACE O&M Logs
selfCheckPillars.subtitle: 33 CFR § 208.10 & Non-NLD Watershed Structures

questions.text: County maintains a complete inventory of all floodwalls, levees, closures, and NRCS watershed channels—including legacy works outside the USACE NLD.
questions.actionItem: Reconcile local municipal floodwalls, WPA channels, and NRCS dams with USACE District (Huntington/Pittsburgh/Baltimore) and Conservation District records.

questions.text: 90-day and pre-flood-season 33 CFR § 208.10 inspection logs (embankments, joints, toe drains, culverts, flap gates) are signed and archived with photos.
questions.actionItem: Schedule quarterly 33 CFR § 208.10 walk-down inspections of all local levees, floodwalls, and flap gates and archive dated geotagged photos.

questions.text: Woody vegetation (>2 in. diameter), encroachments, and animal burrows on levee slopes and within 15 ft of embankment toes are actively cleared and logged.
questions.actionItem: Clear brush/trees from embankment toes and document compacted impervious backfill of any groundhog/muskrat burrows prior to spring thaw.

questions.text: Stormwater pump stations, backup diesel generators, and numbered street/railroad stop-log closures undergo annual full-load & erection drills.
questions.actionItem: Conduct an annual physical stop-log erection drill and 2-hour load-bank/wet-well pump exercise ahead of spring flood season.

questions.text: USACE PL 84-99 Rehabilitation & NRCS EWP 30-day post-flood request templates and 3-year O&M expenditure proof are ready for immediate submission.
questions.actionItem: Pre-stage 30-day USACE PL 84-99 and NRCS EWP sponsor request letters alongside 3-year local O&M maintenance ledgers.

selfCheckPillars.title: 5. Financial Traceability & 2 CFR 200 Clauses
selfCheckPillars.subtitle: SAM.gov, 70-Hour Cap, PPDR ROE & 3-Year Audit Trail

questions.text: Purchasing workflow enforces mandatory timestamped SAM.gov active/non-debarred PDF capture BEFORE executing any disaster contract or task order.
questions.actionItem: Embed a hard checklist gate on every emergency Task Order requiring a timestamped SAM.gov exclusion search PDF prior to Commission signature.

questions.text: 2 CFR Part 200 Appendix II Federal Contract Rider (Termination, Clean Air/Water, Byrd Anti-Lobbying, OIG Records Access) is pre-attached to county forms.
questions.actionItem: Adopt a standardized 2-page 2 CFR Part 200 Appendix II Federal Rider automatically stapled to all county emergency purchase orders.

questions.text: Emergency Time-and-Materials (T&M) task orders enforce a written suitability determination, hard dollar NTE cap, and strict 70-operating-hour cutoff.
questions.actionItem: Pre-print Template A (70-Hour Emergency Roadway Task Order with NTE Cap) in the Courthouse & EOC Emergency Binder.

questions.text: Force account disaster timesheets separate regular straight-time from emergency overtime and Category A (Debris) from Category B (Life Safety).
questions.actionItem: Deploy disaster payroll codes that track Overtime vs. Straight-Time and FEMA Equipment Rate active operating hours per road segment.

questions.text: Digital closeout binder preserves 1:1 load-to-scale-to-check proofs for 3+ years AFTER WVEMD submits final statewide disaster closeout to FEMA.
questions.actionItem: Configure immutable County Clerk cloud/vault retention tied to WVEMD formal statewide FEMA PA disaster closeout notification (+3 years minimum).

wvStatutesAndDoctrine.topic: Governor's State of Emergency & Preparedness Proclamation
wvStatutesAndDoctrine.rule: Authorizes Governor (or Legislature by concurrent resolution) to proclaim a state of emergency; activates emergency powers and state EOP.

wvStatutesAndDoctrine.topic: Local Emergency Organization & Mutual Aid Arrangements
wvStatutesAndDoctrine.rule: Authorizes county/municipal emergency services directors and reciprocal intrastate mutual aid across West Virginia political subdivisions.
Governs interstate mutual aid requests, credential reciprocity, tort liability, and reimbursement through WVEMD.

wvStatutesAndDoctrine.cite: WV HB 5638 / WVOT Cyber Incident Protocol
wvStatutesAndDoctrine.rule: Requires immediate isolation of compromised OT/IT segments, preservation of forensic logs, and coordination with WVOT CISO / WV Fusion Center—prohibits unapproved ransom payments.
EMPG recipients must maintain a progressive HSEEP exercise program and submit a completed After-Action Report / Improvement Plan (AAR/IP) within 90 calendar days.

T&M contracts are restricted to a reasonable initial emergency window (typically <= 70 hours under FEMA PA guidance), require a strict dollar ceiling, and require independent load/scale/monitor verification.
